The real issue isn’t cutting Medicaid—it’s the systemic waste and fraud draining its funds. Bureaucrats have turned healthcare into a bloated mess where billions vanish into administrative black holes and overpriced contracts. 

Take the GAO’s latest findings: over $600 billion in federal spending isn’t even properly tracked, let alone audited. Medicaid’s core problem isn’t funding levels; it’s a broken system that rewards inefficiency. Hospitals overcharge, middlemen inflate costs, and D.C. throws cash at the symptoms instead of the disease. 

Want to fix healthcare? Start by gutting the red tape, exposing price-gouging, and redirecting every dollar to patients—not bureaucrats. Until then, any talk of “cuts” or “funding” is just political theater.
